title: Mock client simulator (scripted fake clients speaking the WS protocol)
goal: Backend developers can script fake clients that speak the full WebSocket protocol (hello, heartbeat, sequenced events, ack, resume, faults) so relay lanes are built and tested with no real client.
scope_in: `SimClient` class: opens a WS with subprotocol `centcom.v1`, sends `sys.hello` within 5 s, parses `sys.welcome`, answers `sys.ping` with `sys.pong`, tracks `seq`, sends `ack` at least every 5 s and after every 64 frames, de-duplicates by `seq`.

Outbound helpers that build valid frames: client-generated `msg_` ids, `event`/`queue`/`control`/`presence` frames with `k` and cleartext `p` or opaque `ct` blobs (random bytes, no real crypto) and a dummy `sig`; resend of unacked frames after reconnect.
Ticket minting for tests: `mintTestTicket()` signs a relay JWT (EdDSA, aud `centcom-relay`, 60 s, jti, claims sid/mid/role/dev/caps) with a test key pair exposed through a test JWKS.
Scenario DSL: `scenario().connect('host').connect('guest').send(...).expect(...)` with timeouts, plus `SimFleet` to run N clients (up to 50).

Fault injection: drop/duplicate/delay/reorder inbound frames, force disconnect with a chosen close code, stall the socket, send malformed JSON, oversize frames (>256 KiB), send before hello, send `from`/`seq` fields (must be ignored by the server).
Loopback reference server `LoopbackRelay` (test-only, in-process) implementing handshake, seq assignment and echo, used to test the simulator itself.
scope_out: The real relay (relay lanes from B037 on); LoopbackRelay is only for self-tests and must not be exported for production.
Real end-to-end encryption (CT-CRYPTO is client-implemented; the simulator uses opaque ciphertext).
Load testing at scale (later infra lane).
build_against: Run against LoopbackRelay inside the package; the same SimClient later targets the real relay via `ws://localhost:<port>/v1/ws`. Frames are validated with @centcom/contracts validators (B003) against contracts/fixtures/events.
interfaces: `class SimClient { static connect(opts:{url: string; ticket: string; protocols?: number[]; caps?: string[]; lastSeq?: number|null; clock?: Clock}): Promise<SimClient>; send(kind: string, p?: object, opts?:{ct?: boolean; type?: 'event'|'queue'|'control'}): Promise<{id: string; seq: number}>; sendRaw(data: string): void; waitFor(pred: (f: Frame) => boolean, timeoutMs?: number): Promise<Frame>; frames: readonly Frame[]; lastSeq: number; close(code?: number): Promise<void>; reconnect(): Promise<void> }`.
`mintTestTicket(opts:{sid: string; mid: string; role: 'host'|'editor'|'viewer'; dev: string; ttlS?: number}): Promise<string>` and `testJwks(): JsonWebKeySet`.
`class SimFleet { static spawn(n: number, make: (i: number) => ConnectOpts): Promise<SimFleet> }`.
`faults.drop(p) | faults.duplicate(p) | faults.delay(ms) | faults.reorder(window) | faults.disconnectAfter(n, code)` as socket middleware.
Defaults mirror the contract: ping_ms 20000, dead_ms 50000, hello timeout 5000, ack every 64 frames / 5 s.
acceptance: SimClient completes the handshake against LoopbackRelay and exposes the `welcome` fields member, role, heartbeat.ping_ms=20000, dead_ms=50000.
Sending 200 sequenced frames from two clients yields a strictly increasing `seq` starting at 1 in both clients' received logs, with no gaps.

After `disconnectAfter(50, 1006)` and `reconnect()`, the client sends `last_seq` equal to its highest contiguous processed seq and resends its unacked frames with the same `id`; the loopback de-dups to exactly one copy.
With `faults.duplicate(1.0)` the client's `frames` contains each seq once while the raw wire had two copies.
`sendRaw('{not json')` makes LoopbackRelay respond with `sys.error`; after more than 10 invalid frames in a minute the test observes close code 4400.
A client that does not send `sys.hello` within 5 s is closed with 4408 (fake clock advances time; the test runs in under 1 s real time).
A frame of 262 145 bytes (256 KiB + 1) is rejected with `sys.error` code `invalid_frame` in LoopbackRelay.
All frames the simulator emits validate against the envelope schema (checked on every send in debug mode).
tests: heartbeat.test.ts and sequencing.test.ts: fake-timer ping/pong, ack cadence, seq monotonicity with two clients.
resume.test.ts and faults.test.ts: reconnect with last_seq, resend of unacked frames, drop/duplicate/reorder/malformed/oversize.
fixture-conformance.test.ts: every contracts/fixtures/events frame can be sent by SimClient and echoed back unmodified except server-set fields.
guardrails: MUST NOT set server-owned fields (`from`, `ts`, `seq`) on outbound frames except in explicit fault scenarios that assert the server ignores them.
MUST keep test signing keys in the testkit only (kid prefix `test-`); the relay under test must be configured with the test JWKS so these keys can never validate against a production JWKS.
MUST NOT implement or fake real encryption; ciphertext is opaque random bytes so no one mistakes the simulator for a crypto reference.
MUST bound every wait with a timeout (default 5 s) and every buffer (frames log capped at 10 000 entries) so a hung relay fails a test instead of hanging CI.
MUST NOT export LoopbackRelay from the package root index (separate `@centcom/testkit/sim` entry).
failure_modes: Server closes with 4401/4403/4404/4426 -> SimClient does not auto-reconnect and surfaces the code to the test.
Server closes with other codes -> reconnect only on explicit `reconnect()` so tests stay deterministic (optional `autoReconnect` mirrors the contract: 250 ms x 2^n, full jitter, cap 15 s).
Unknown frame type or kind received -> logged at debug, acked, ignored (robustness rule).
notes: SPLIT? L-sized: if time-boxed, ship client + ticket + loopback first and fleet/faults as a follow-up PR.
